papers.title: Quantitative global regularity for Navier--Stokes equations with odd viscosity on the cubic three-torus
papers.summary: We study the three-dimensional incompressible Navier--Stokes equation on the cubic torus with a constant odd-viscosity operator given by the vertical derivative of the curl. Arbitrary real, mean-zero, divergence-free initial data and an independent steady force, both in the second-order Sobolev space, admit a unique global strong solution when the magnitude of one fixed odd-viscosity coefficient is at least a norm-uniform sufficient threshold. In the unforced case the solution is smooth at positive times. The qualitative argument adapts the resonant-averaging framework for rapidly rotating fluids to the different odd-viscous dispersion. Weighted lattice counts and signed corrected-energy estimates yield a sufficient bound for the odd-to-ordinary viscosity ratio that is polynomial in the normalized initial-data radius at each fixed normalized force radius, together with a separate bound in a specified force-dominated regime. No optimality is claimed for the polynomial exponents or prefactors; determining the sharp viscosity threshold for the original equation remains open. Direct kinetic and weighted enstrophy barriers also give regularity for every coefficient on explicit bounded data and force regions, including the closed unforced ball of homogeneous second-order Fourier Sobolev radius ninety-seven fortieths times the viscosity and seven closed forced rectangles. We specify how finite certificates enter the analytic argument and distinguish minimization of a sufficient formula from sharpness for the original equation. All three main theorems are formally verified in Lean 4 with Mathlib.

papers.title: Delaunay Asymptotics for the Singular Escobar-Yamabe Equation
papers.summary: In dimensions $n\geq3$, we prove that near an isolated boundary singularity a positive solution of the Escobar--Yamabe equation for a smooth metric approaches a fixed periodic Delaunay solution or the cylindrical solution if its trace lies between positive multiples of $|\overline x|^{-(n-2)/2}$, where $\overline x$ is the tangential Fermi coordinate. The relative error decays at a positive power rate, with weighted estimates through two derivatives in Fermi coordinates. The necksize is unique, and the translation parameter is unique modulo the least positive period in the periodic case. The Hamiltonian smoothly parametrizes the periodic family modulo translation. We classify Jacobi fields of polynomial growth at both ends without assuming symmetry. Translation and energy differentiation generate these fields along periodic solutions, and two oscillatory fields generate them along the cylindrical solution. We also exhibit a first-order obstruction to improving these asymptotics by boundary-preserving conformal deformations of the flat models.

papers.title: Stability of patterns in variational systems with continuous symmetries: a computer-assisted approach
papers.summary: In variational models of pattern formation, periodic solutions are never isolated: since the energy does not change under translations, every shifted copy of a pattern is again a solution. This is an obstacle for computer-assisted proofs, which need isolated solutions. Imposing discrete symmetries removes the obstacle, but restricts the patterns that can be studied and only gives stability against symmetric perturbations. We develop a computer-assisted method that deals with the translations directly. We fix the position of the pattern with phase conditions and add unfolding parameters. They act as Lagrange multipliers, and translation invariance of the energy ensures that they vanish at a solution, under a condition that is verified rigorously by the computer. We then derive the stability of the pattern from the computer-assisted proof. We obtain the number of unstable directions and show that the only neutral directions are the translations. We apply the method to the Swift-Hohenberg equation in two dimensions and prove the existence of stable and unstable patterns without imposed symmetry. Since the linear algebra does not depend on the number of translation directions, the approach extends to higher dimensions.

papers.title: On regularity and stability results of global weak solutions to two-dimensional Navier-Stokes equations with density-dependent viscosity and vacuum
papers.summary: For the initial and initial-boundary value problems of the two-dimensional (2D) incompressible Navier-Stokes equations with density-dependent viscosity and vacuum, Lions' global weak solutions are shown to possess additional regularity, via establishing some key a priori decay-in-time rates for the approximate problem, under suitable smallness condition on the density-dependent viscosity. In addition, large-time decay rates of the pressure and gradient of velocity are obtained, which are even exponential in time for bounded domains or the periodic case. Note that these results hold without any smallness conditions on the initial data, even for initially vanishing density.

papers.title: The Cheng--Yau gradient estimate for Jacobi fields
papers.summary: We prove a pointwise gradient estimate for positive Jacobi fields on minimal hypersurfaces of dimension two and three, inspired by the Cheng--Yau estimate for harmonic functions. The estimate also controls the second fundamental form, and so provides yet another proof of the stable Bernstein theorem in dimensions two and three.

papers.title: A Large Gap between Galerkin Errors with and without Mesh-Uniform Regularity for the KdV Equation with Boundary Dissipation
papers.summary: We compare two cubic Hermite Galerkin semidiscretizations of the Korteweg-de Vries equation on a bounded interval with boundary dissipation. They use the same trial space. The first is the weighted scheme considered in our previous paper (arXiv:2610.39269), called the W-scheme. It has mesh-uniform regularity: the discrete semigroups of the linearized equation inherit Crandall-Pazy regularity and Kato smoothing, with bounds uniform in the mesh size $h$. The second is the standard Galerkin method in $L^2$, called the S-scheme. It has no mesh-uniform regularity. For the W-scheme, the full error and the ordering error converge at an algebraic rate in $h$, uniformly on $[t_0,\infty)$ times small balls of $L^2$ for any fixed $t_0>0$. They are bounded by $Ch^p\varepsilon$ and $Ch^p\varepsilon^2$, respectively, where $\varepsilon$ is the size of the datum and $p>0$. We prove that neither bound holds for the S-scheme by using exact high-frequency spurious eigenpairs of the S-scheme. The existence of such eigenpairs for fine meshes with at least 512 elements has a proof checked by Lean 4. Computations compare the two schemes on unit-norm data built from these eigenfunctions, on 512, 1024 and 2048 elements. The full error of the S-scheme stays at $4.6\times10^{-2}$. That of the W-scheme is at most $2.2\times10^{-9}$. The ordering error of the S-scheme stays at $9.6\times10^{-6}$. That of the W-scheme falls from $2.3\times10^{-9}$ to $1.4\times10^{-10}$. Their ratio grows from $4.2\times10^3$ to $6.6\times10^4$.
papers.comment: 44 pages, 2 figures. Ancillary files: the Lean 4 development for Theorem 3.1, and the programs, outputs and logs of the computations

papers.title: Single-point determination of a potential and a nonlinearity in a semilinear biharmonic equation
papers.summary: In this paper, we study the inverse problem of determining the coefficient $q$ and the nonlinearity $F$ in the semilinear biharmonic equation $Δ^2 u+q(x)u=F(x,u)$ with Navier boundary data. The measurement consists of $\partial_νu(x_0)$ at a fixed boundary point $x_0$. We apply the mixed variation approach to linearize the nonlinear problem and construct semiclassical boundary-localized solutions for the linearized equation. Under suitable analyticity, nonresonance, and nondegeneracy assumptions on $q$ and $F$, we prove that this boundary point measurement uniquely determines both $q$ and $F$. We also establish boundary determination of all normal derivatives of $q$ and of the first nonzero Taylor coefficient of $F$ on a nonempty relatively open subset of the boundary. When the linear potential $q$ is known, we prove that either component of the Navier boundary input alone suffices to determine $F$, and that the polynomial nonlinearity can be uniquely determined without requiring any analyticity conditions. For suitable finite-dimensional classes of nonanalytic potentials, we also obtain, for fixed $F$, the stable determination of $q$ from finitely many boundary inputs and the associated point measurements. In addition, as an important supplement, we provide nontrivial examples verifying the main assumptions, as well as counterexamples concerning the recovery of the linear coefficient. Finally, we present numerical experiments that demonstrate the theoretical results.

papers.title: Exponential mixing for the randomized two-vortex model
papers.summary: This paper investigates the mixing of passive scalars advected by a randomized two-vortex model on $\mathbb{T}^2$, in which the vortices interact through a regularized Biot--Savart kernel and are driven by independent Brownian motions. We establish quenched exponential mixing for the Lagrangian flow, characterized by the exponential correlation decay of mean-zero $H^s$ observables. The proof proceeds by establishing ergodicity of the associated two-point Markov process. We combine a uniform contraction estimate with controllability arguments to verify the Lyapunov drift and minorization conditions, allowing us to apply Harris-type theorem.

papers.title: Existence of a non-zero steady-state solution to a population density equation subject to horizontal transfer
papers.summary: From plasmid dynamics and efflux pump expression in bacteria to risk-taking behaviour in human groups, horizontal interactions can drive the transmission of deleterious traits that spread despite carrying no selective advantage, thereby burdening the population. How can such detrimental traits persist, and under what conditions can the population avoid extinction? To address these questions, we model a population structured by a continuous trait representing individual burden within a non-linear, non-local integro-differential framework. From an analytical perspective, mutations are modeled via a jump operator rather than a diffusion term; consequently, the mutation operator lacks regularizing properties and is generally non-self-adjoint. Moreover, working in a weighted L 1 setting precludes the direct application of standard Krein-Rutman theory. To overcome these hurdles, we construct a custom fixed-point operator by first freezing the non-linearities to solve an auxiliary eigenvalue problem, and then tuning the resulting principal eigenvalue. Applying the Leray-Schauder fixed-point theorem to this operator rigorously yields the existence of a non-trivial steady state. Finally, numerical simulations illustrate the qualitative dynamics of the model and delineate the parameter regimes governing population persistence and extinction.

papers.title: Non-connected minimal clusters of small volume in a compact Finsler manifold
papers.summary: We prove that isoperimetric clusters in general Finsler manifolds can be disconnected even when the volume constraint is small. This is in contrast with the Riemannian case and the ``fixed-norm'' case, where connectedness for arbitrarily small volume has recently been proved.

papers.title: Microlocal properties of Cauchy evolution under metric variations
papers.summary: We develop the microlocal analysis of the Cauchy evolution for wave-type equations on the infinite-dimensional space of Lorentzian metrics. We regard the Cauchy evolution operator as a distributional function of the metric, and give this notion a precise meaning through restrictions to finite-dimensional families of metrics. We study the singularities of this metric dependence. For normally hyperbolic operators on vector bundles, we determine the resulting operator-valued wavefront sets. Their parameter covectors are given by integrals of metric variations along individual null geodesics. At ultrastatic ends, metric dependence also determines the time-translation generators and their positive- and negative-energy splitting. More generally, the parameter singularities distinguish the two characteristic sheets and can be used to reconstruct the ordinary Cauchy propagation relation, which describes propagation of singularities. Consequences include smoothing under parameter averaging and polar-cone bounds associated with averaged null-positive variations, linking the result to averaged null energy conditions. The analysis also covers the Cauchy evolution of the Dirac equation.

papers.title: An almost sharp tomas-stein restriction theorem for a class of anisotropic operators
papers.summary: Let $d\geq 2$. For each $j\in \{1,\dots,d\}$, let ${\ell}_{j}\geq 1$ and $m_{j}\geq 2$ be integers, and let $a_{j}$ be a nonzero real number. We prove that the oscillatory integral operator \begin{equation*} T_{{\ell}_{1},\dots,{\ell}_{d},m_{1},\dots,m_{d}}f(x):=\int_{\mathbb{R}^{d}} e^{\dot{\imath} \left(a_{1}x^{{\ell}_{1}}_{1}y^{m_{1}}_{1}+\dots +a_{d}x^{{\ell}_{d}}_{d}y^{m_{d}}_{d} \right)}f(y)dy,\;\;\; x\in \mathbb{R}^{d}, \end{equation*} satisfies the restriction estimate \begin{equation*} \|T_{{\ell}_{1},\dots,{\ell}_{d},m_{1},\dots,m_{d}}f\|_{L^{2}(\mathbb{S}^{d-1})}\lesssim \|f\|_{L^{p}(\mathbb{R}^{d})}, \end{equation*} for each $1\leq p\leq 2$, whenever $(\frac{\ell_{j}}{m_{j}}-\frac{1}{m_{j}}+1)\frac{2}{p^{\prime}}\geq 1$, for every $j\in Γ$, and \begin{equation*} \mathcal{E}:=\min{\left\{\min_{1\leq j\leq d}{\frac{m_{j}}{{\ell}_{j}}},\,\min_{1\leq k\leq d}{\frac{d-1}{\sum_{j\neq k} \frac{\ell_{j}}{m_{j}}+\frac{2}{m_{k}}}}\right\}}> \frac{2}{p^{\prime}}. \end{equation*} We also give counterexamples that show that the condition $\mathcal{E}\geq 2/p^{\prime}$ is necessary for this restriction inequality.

papers.title: Branch Obstructions for Area-Minimizing Currents and Flat Critical Points of Weakly-Conformal Maps
papers.summary: We study two problems motivated by the local geometry of conformal $φ$-curves. First, let $T$ be a $k$-dimensional locally area-minimizing integral current in Euclidean space, with $k\geq3$, codimension at least two, no boundary, and a locally conformally flat induced metric on $\operatorname{reg} T$. We prove the following branch obstruction: at any rapid-decay branch point whose planar frequency differs from $2$, every nonzero cyclic component of every cylindrical normalized tangent function has repetition multiplicity at least two. Consequently, the nonintegral-frequency points of densities $2$ and $3$ in the rapid-decay branch set have Hausdorff dimension at most $k-3$. On the full branch set, they have zero $\mathcal H^{k-2}$ measure. These conclusions apply to Euclidean image currents of conformal $φ$-curves with locally conformally flat domains, provided the image currents satisfy the stated hypotheses. Second, for $C^j$ weakly-conformal maps between smooth Riemannian manifolds, with domain dimension $k\geq3$ and $j\geq2$, we prove that all derivatives of orders $1$ through $j$ vanish at every critical point. As a consequence, for smooth weakly-conformal maps with connected domain, we establish a curvature condition under which the map is constant or has no critical points. The flatness and continuation results apply in particular to conformal $φ$-curves with the corresponding regularity and curvature assumptions. Finally, we examine the Borůvka cone, which illustrates the role of regularity and the distinction between critical points and branch points.

papers.title: A capillary logarithmic Gauss curvature flow and the capillary Minkowski problem
papers.summary: We study a logarithmic Gauss curvature flow of strictly convex capillary hypersurfaces in the Euclidean half-space. For an acute contact angle and an arbitrary positive smooth prescribed function, we prove that a suitable initial dilation yields a global solution which converges smoothly after a horizontal translation with a uniquely determined constant velocity. As an application, we provide a logarithmic flow proof of the capillary Minkowski problem, previously established by Mei-Wang-Weng [Adv. Math. 469, 110230 (2025)].

papers.title: Positive solutions of power equations in planar corner domains
papers.summary: We study positive solutions of $Δu=λu^k$ on bounded planar corner domains with zero boundary values away from the vertex. For negative-power absorption we identify the admissible interval of Martin masses and prove uniqueness at the minimum mass. Along the ordinary boundary, we identify the weak Hessian endpoint and its sharp tail when the set of zero inward derivative has positive length. For superlinear sources we prove attainment of the largest positive Martin mass in the subcritical range. At criticality we construct a family of singular solutions with zero Martin mass and distinguish its members by their second logarithmic coefficient and the endpoint integrability of their Hessian differences. Above criticality an angular eigenvalue governs the Morse index away from its zero threshold. We also give sharp physical-Hessian asymptotics for finite-mass remainders and joint corner and side estimates for negative-power sources.

papers.title: A Silverman-Meadows-type criterion for the null controllability of time-dependent coupled heat equations with non-diagonalizable diffusion matrices
papers.summary: This paper is devoted to a uniform spectral Silverman-Meadows rank condition for the nullcontrollability of coupled systems of heat equations with time-dependent diffusion, coupling and control matrices. The proof relies on an adaptation of the Lebeau-Robbiano strategy combined with uniform finite-dimensional observability estimates associated with each Laplace eigenmode.

papers.title: Persistence in weighted Sobolev spaces for the Calogero-Moser derivative nonlinear Schrödinger equation
papers.summary: This paper is devoted to the study of invariant weighted Sobolev spaces for the Calogero--Moser derivative nonlinear Schrödinger (CMDNLS) equation on the real line. For \(s\geq 1\) and \(0\leq r\leq s\), we first prove that the \(H^s(\mathbb R)\) flow preserves the condition \((1+x^2)^{r/2}u\in L^2(\mathbb R)\). The proof uses truncated weighted energy estimates and weighted interpolation. We then establish the persistence of weighted regularity for spatial derivatives. For integers \(p\geq 3\) and \(1\leq m\leq p-2\), and for \(0\leq r\leq p-m \), the \(H^p(\mathbb R)\) flow preserves the conditions \((1+x^2)^{r/2}\partial_x^j u\in L^2(\mathbb R)\) for \(0\leq j\leq m\). This result combines weighted energy estimates, the unitary equivalence and the integrable structure of the CMDNLS equation.

papers.title: On the Abels--Garcke--Grün Model for Incompressible Two-Phase Flows with Unmatched Densities: Phase Separation and Rayleigh--Taylor Instability
papers.summary: Instability phenomena are ubiquitous in multi-fluid flows. For binary fluid mixtures, phase separation may occur under specific conditions, in which a homogeneous state becomes unstable and spontaneously segregates into different phases, leading to the formation of distinct patterns. Furthermore, when a heavier fluid is superposed over a lighter one in a gravitational field, the fluid interface can be sensitive to perturbations that trigger the Rayleigh--Taylor (RT) instability, i.e., the lighter fluid penetrates upward into the heavier fluid against gravity. We investigate such instability phenomena and the inhibiting conditions for incompressible, immiscible two-phase flows with unmatched densities, within the framework of a diffuse-interface model, which is called the Abels--Garcke--Grün (AGG) model. More precisely, we adopt energy methods to establish several stability/instability conditions for the perturbed system of the AGG model, which is obtained by slightly perturbing the equilibrium profile $(\mathbf{0},\overline{\varphi})$, where $\overline{\varphi}=\overline{\varphi}(x_3)$ depends solely on the vertical coordinate $x_3$. Notably, for a constant equilibrium profile $\overline{\varphi}=α\in(-1,1)$ satisfying $Ψ''(α)<0$, we establish a threshold for stability and instability of the phase-separation problem.Similar stability results are also established for the perturbed system with $\overline{\varphi}$ satisfying the RT instability condition in the presence of gravity. In particular, if the phase-separation condition fails and $\partial_{x_3}\overline{\varphi}$ is a constant, a larger value of $\partial_{x_3}\overline{\varphi}$, a greater interfacial thickness and a higher surface energy density contribute to inhibiting RT instability.

papers.title: Asymptotic spreading of Fisher-KPP equations in shifting environments with time-periodic limits
papers.summary: In this paper, we study the rightward spreading speed of solutions for Fisher-KPP equations in shifting environments. The linear growth rate has time periodic limits at the two ends of the moving frame. Each limit has a positive average and may be negative during a period. When the growth rate lies between the two limits at each time, we show that the spreading speed depends only on their averages and the asymptotic shift speed. For intermediate shift speeds, the formulas give nonlocal pulling if the right end has the larger average and speed locking if the left end has the larger average. The interior growth profile may be nonmonotone in space and aperiodic in time. We prove the formulas by constructing upper and lower solutions for a stepwise profile and then comparing with shifted stepwise problems.

papers.title: Resonances of the Kramers-Fokker-Planck Operator
papers.summary: We study the subellipticity of the analytically deformed Kramers-Fokker-Planck operator and give two definitions of resonances, one based on analytic dilation and the other on analytic distortion in the $x$-variables. Due to the failure of global subellipticity of the distorted operator in dimensions $n \geq 2$, the second method can only be used in dimension one. We show that, whenever both methods are applicable, they give rise to the same set of resonances. We also prove that, when $|\na V(x)| = O(\w x^{-ρ})$ with $ρ>1$, positive resonances are embedded eigenvalues and/or scattering resonances whose resonant states belong to weighted $L^2$-spaces and satisfy an outgoing radiation condition.

papers.title: Generation of semigroups for vector-valued pseudodifferential operators on the torus with space-dependent symbols
papers.summary: We consider toroidal pseudodifferential operators with spatially dependent, operator-valued symbols of positive order and finite regularity. For an arbitrary complex Banach space $E$, we prove that the negative of the closure of a parabolic operator on $C^\infty(\mathbb T^n,E)$ generates an analytic semigroup on $W_p^k(\mathbb T^n,E)$, where $1\le p<\infty$ and $k\in\mathbb N_0$, provided the symbol has sufficiently many spatial derivatives and discrete differences. The proof combines uniform estimates for parameter-dependent kernels with right and left parametrices. It does not require the UMD property of $E$. Real interpolation gives corresponding resolvent estimates on $B_{pq}^s(\mathbb T^n,E)$ for $0<s<k$ and $1\le q\le\infty$. The induced semigroups are strongly continuous for $q<\infty$ and on the little Besov spaces when $q=\infty$.

papers.title: Lie-Lions brackets of nonlocal vector fields
papers.summary: We study nonlocal vector fields on the space of probability measures with finite second moment. Using Lions derivatives, we define their Lie-Lions bracket, which adds to the spatial Lie bracket a correction due to the evolution of the law, and prove that its vanishing is equivalent to commutation of the global flows, under first-order regularity and linear growth assumptions. We then construct a Lie algebra of complete polynomial nonlocal fields. For this class, we establish commutator and second-order Baker-Campbell-Hausdorff formulas with cubic remainders in the Wasserstein distance $W_2$, controlled by the second moment and uniform in the number of particles. The proofs rely on finite-particle realizations, which preserve the bracket and jointly determine the nonlocal field. We also obtain uniform estimates for smooth bounded kernels and a Leibniz rule for the action of polynomial fields on polynomial observables. Examples from collective dynamics show that the vanishing of the spatial bracket at a fixed law is neither necessary nor sufficient for commutation. They concern symmetries, aggregation-dependent rotation, synchronization, the transmission of a turn along a hierarchy, effective three-body interactions and occupancy-dependent circulation.

papers.title: Smooth asymptotically Self-similar blow up for the scalar Zakharov system in dimension $3$
papers.summary: We construct blow up solutions to the scalar Zakharov system in dimension $3$. More precisely, we construct the solutions $(ψ,n)$ defined for $t\in[0,T)$, blowing up at $t=T$ and taking the form \begin{align} ψ(t,x) \sim\frac{1}{T-t}P\left(\frac{|x|}{\sqrt{3}(T-t)^{\frac{2}{3}}}\right)e^{i(T-t)^{-1/3}}, n(t,x) \sim\frac{1}{3(T-t)^{4/3}}N\left(\frac{|x|}{\sqrt{3}(T-t)^{\frac{2}{3}}}\right) \end{align} in the region $|x|\ll 1$. Here $(P,N)$ is the solution to a specified ODE system related to Zakharov system. The solutions we construct are smooth for $0\leq t<T$. Moreover, there exist $n_0,n_1\in C^{\infty}(\mathbb{R}^3\backslash\{0\})$ with bounded support such that for any $r>0$, $(ψ,n,\partial_t n)$ converge to $(0,n_0,n_1)$ in $C^{\infty}(|x|>r)$. We correct the profile $(P,N)$ and obtain a sequence of approximate solutions that coincide in the region $|x|\gtrsim 1$ with higher and higher accuracy. Then we apply perturbative analysis to construct solutions with arbitrarily high finite regularity. The fixed point argument in this procedure actually yields that these solutions are the same for $t$ sufficiently close to $T$, which combined with the persistence of high regularity gives the existence of smooth asymptotically self-similar blow up solutions.

papers.title: Uniqueness of positive solutions of mixed Laplacian and fractional Laplacian in $\mathbb R$
papers.summary: We establish the uniqueness and nondegeneracy for positive finite-energy solutions of the following one-dimensional mixed Schrödinger equation \begin{equation} -Q'' + (-Δ)^s Q + Q = |Q|^p Q \quad \text{in } \mathbb R, \end{equation} where $0<s<1$ and $p>0$. For every $0<s<1, p>0$, we obtain the corresponding results for positive solutions whose linearized operators have Morse index equal to one. We extend the nodal analysis developed by Frank-Lenzmann-Silvestre to the mixed operator establishing the monotonicity of the quotient of a hypothetical nontrivial even kernel element by $-Q'$. We then combine this monotonicity with oscillation estimates to prove nondegeneracy, and uniqueness follows by continuation. Moreover, for every $1/2\le s<1,p>0$, both uniqueness and nondegeneracy hold for positive solutions. Our novelty is to use the properties of Green kernel of the mixed operator to derive the upper bound and lower bound on the maximum of each solution. This peak estimate allows us to prove uniqueness by direct comparison and to establish nondegeneracy.

papers.title: BMO Vorticity Strong Ill-Posedness for the 2d Incompressible Euler Equation
papers.summary: For the two dimensional incompressible Euler equation, Yudovich, and independently Serfati, extended the classical existence and uniqueness class to include vorticity with mild singularity. This class is sometimes called the generalized Yudovich class. Then, Vishik extended the uniqueness class to include vorticity in BMO, allowing for stronger singularities than the generalized Yudovich class. In this work, we prove strong ill-posedness of vorticity in BMO.
